title: WHO Emergency & Essential Surgical Care Guidelines: Appendicitis Protocol
content: Acute appendicitis presents classically with periumbilical abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant (McBurney point) within 12 to 24 hours. Accompanied by low-grade fever, anorexia, nausea, and localized peritoneal rebound tenderness. Prompt surgical evaluation or emergency abdominal ultrasound/CT is indicated to prevent perforation and peritonitis.

title: AHA / ESC Guidelines for Acute Chest Pain Management
content: Retrosternal chest pressure, tightness, or heavy sensation radiating to the left arm, jaw, or epigastrium lasting >20 minutes, accompanied by diaphoresis, dyspnea, or presyncope, constitutes high-risk Acute Coronary Syndrome. Immediate 12-lead ECG, troponin testing, and emergency resuscitation protocol activation are mandatory.

title: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia
content: Preeclampsia with severe features is characterized by systolic BP >= 160 mmHg or diastolic BP >= 110 mmHg after 20 weeks gestation, paired with persistent severe headache, visual disturbances (scotoma, blurred vision), right upper quadrant abdominal pain, or thrombocytopenia. Requires immediate emergency obstetric admission, IV magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis, and controlled antihypertensive therapy.

title: American Dental Association (ADA) Clinical Pathway: Odontogenic Infections
content: Odontogenic periapical abscess presents with severe localized throbbing tooth pain, facial or submandibular edema, fever, and tender regional lymphadenopathy. If airway compromise, trismus (<20mm opening), or systemic toxicity develops, urgent surgical drainage and parenteral antibiotic therapy are indicated within 12-24 hours.

title: NICE Guidelines NG138: Pneumonia in Adults Diagnosis and Management
content: Community-acquired pneumonia manifests as acute cough, purulent sputum, fever > 38°C, pleuritic chest pain, and focal crackles or bronchial breathing on auscultation. CURB-65 severity score stratification dictates ambulatory versus inpatient oral or intravenous antibiotic therapy.

title: AHA / ASA Guidelines for Management of Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
content: Sudden onset severe headache reaching peak intensity within seconds ('thunderclap headache'), often described as the worst headache of life, frequently associated with neck stiffness, photophobia, vomiting, or altered consciousness. Demands emergency non-contrast cranial CT and lumbar puncture.

title: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of GERD
content: GERD presents with postprandial retrosternal burning (heartburn) and acidic regurgitation, typically exacerbated by recumbency or greasy meals. Empirical trial of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and lifestyle modification (head elevation, avoiding late meals) are initial first-line approaches.

title: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193: Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy
content: First-trimester pelvic pain accompanied by irregular vaginal bleeding and cervical motion tenderness requires immediate exclusion of tubal ectopic pregnancy via quantitative beta-hCG and transvaginal ultrasound. Hemoperitoneum from ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy causes shoulder tip pain and hypovolemic shock requiring emergency laparoscopy.

title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines 2021
content: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. SOFA / qSOFA indicators include systolic BP <= 100 mmHg, respiratory rate >= 22/min, and altered mental status. Requires emergency protocol activation within 1 hour: IV broad-spectrum antibiotics, blood cultures, and fluid resuscitation.

title: EAU Guidelines on Paediatric & Adult Urology: Acute Scrotum
content: Acute testicular torsion manifests as sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain, high-riding testicle with transverse lie, and loss of cremasteric reflex. Requires emergency surgical exploration and detorsion within 6 hours to preserve testicular viability.

title: AAO Preferred Practice Pattern: Primary Angle Closure
content: Sudden severe periocular pain, blurred vision, rainbow-colored halos around light sources, red eye, steamy cornea, mid-dilated fixed pupil, nausea, and headache. Demands immediate intraocular pressure-lowering topical/systemic agents and urgent laser peripheral iridotomy.

title: WHO Guidelines for Malaria Diagnosis and Treatment
content: Malaria presents with paroxysmal high fever, severe rigors/shaking chills, diaphoresis, headache, myalgia, and fatigue. Plasmodium falciparum species risk rapid progression to cerebral malaria, severe anemia, or acute renal failure. Diagnosis requires immediate blood smear microscopic examination or Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT).
